_evidence_Córdova la Llana: Sancho Llerena's marriage act, Canelones, 8 January 1791 (DGS 8166578, image 2687): 'natural de Cordova la Llana'. The baptism of his son Luis Escolástico, Iglesia Matriz, Montevideo, 10 February 1811, calls him 'natural de Andalucia'; the Montevideo census gives his birthplace as 'ANDALUZIA'. So his Córdova is Córdoba in Andalusia, Spain (the story, chapter on the 1791 act; work list: 'la Llana' tells it from Córdoba del Tucumán).
_evidence_Córdoba: The same 1791 act calls Félix Llerena and Rosalía Aguilar 'naturales de dicha Cordova': the said Córdova, their son's, which the 1811 act places in Andalusia. The story's card prints it as 'Córdoba' for both. Spain, by the same evidence; the town itself still rests on that one phrase.
_evidence_the River Plate: Juan Carlos Lerena's card infers only 'the River Plate' (two names on his son's Argentine army card, no other record); its two banks are Uruguay and Argentina today, so no flag.
